Create a complete single self-contained file `chip8_anthropic-claude-sonnet-5_01.html` (HTML + CSS + JavaScript inline;
no external libraries, CDNs, assets or backend). Build a working CHIP-8 emulator.

Implement the interpreter properly: 4 KB of memory with the font set loaded at 0x050 and programs at 0x200,
sixteen 8-bit registers V0 to VF, the 16-bit index register, the program counter, a call stack, and the
delay and sound timers counting down at 60 Hz. Decode and execute the complete instruction set of 35
instructions, including the arithmetic and logic group with the carry and borrow flags in VF, the shift
instructions, jumps and calls, the random instruction, BCD conversion, register save and load, and the key
tests.

The display is 64 by 32 pixels drawn on a canvas scaled to a readable size, with sprites drawn by XOR and
the collision flag set in VF. The 16-key keypad is mapped to a 4 by 4 block of keyboard keys shown in the
interface; key press and release must both reach the emulator.

Include a small demo ROM as a byte array inside the file: a real program, assembled by you, that draws a
sprite and moves or reacts to a key, so that the emulator can be tried without any download. Also allow
loading a ROM from a local file.

Add run, pause, single step and reset controls, an adjustable instructions-per-frame speed, and a debugger
panel showing the registers, the index register, the program counter, the stack and the decoded current
instruction. Every visible control must work. Deliver the one file `chip8_anthropic-claude-sonnet-5_01.html`.

{"path":"chip8_anthropic-claude-sonnet-5_01.html","edit_description":"
Create a complete, self-contained CHIP-8 emulator as a single HTML file (no external resources). Requirements:

STRUCTURE: One HTML file with inline <style> and inline <script>, no external libs/CDNs/assets/backend.

INTERPRETER:
- 4096 bytes memory (Uint8Array). Fontset (standard CHIP-8 4x5 hex digit font, 16 chars x 5 bytes = 80 bytes) loaded at address 0x050.
- Programs loaded starting at 0x200.
- 16 general purpose 8-bit registers V0-VF (Uint8Array(16)).
- 16-bit index register I.
- 16-bit program counter PC, starting at 0x200.
- Call stack: array (or Uint16Array(16)) with stack pointer SP.
- Delay timer (DT) and sound timer (ST), both decremented at 60Hz via a separate timer loop (use setInterval at ~60Hz or accumulate via requestAnimationFrame delta time), independent from the CPU instructions-per-frame execution speed.
- Display: 64x32 monochrome pixel buffer (Uint8Array of 2048), rendered to a <canvas> scaled with CSS/canvas width/height (e.g. each pixel drawn as a 10x10 block, scale configurable via a constant) so it is clearly readable. Use image-rendering: pixelated and no smoothing.
- Keypad: 16 keys (0-F) mapped to the standard CHIP-8 keyboard layout:
  1 2 3 4       1 2 3 C
  Q W E R  -->  4 5 6 D
  A S D F       7 8 9 E
  Z X C V       A 0 B F
  Implement as a Uint8Array(16) keys state. Hook both keydown and keyup window listeners (preventDefault on mapped keys) so press AND release both update emulator key state. Also render a 4x4 grid of on-screen buttons in the UI labeled with the CHIP-8 hex key values; clicking/touching (mousedown/mouseup + touchstart/touchend) these buttons must also set/clear the corresponding key state, and the currently-held keys should be visually highlighted (e.g. a CSS 'active' class) whether triggered by physical keyboard or on-screen button.

FULL OPCODE SET (decode via standard nibble extraction: op = (hi<<8)|lo, n1=hi>>4 etc.), implement all of:
00E0 CLS, 00EE RET, 0NNN (ignore / treat as no-op for legacy SYS), 1NNN JP addr, 2NNN CALL addr,
3XNN SE Vx,byte, 4XNN SNE Vx,byte, 5XY0 SE Vx,Vy, 6XNN LD Vx,byte, 7XNN ADD Vx,byte (no carry affects VF),
8XY0 LD Vx,Vy, 8XY1 OR (set VF=0 per modern quirk optional, just do OR), 8XY2 AND, 8XY3 XOR,
8XY4 ADD Vx,Vy with VF=carry, 8XY5 SUB Vx,Vy with VF=NOT borrow (1 if Vx>=Vy else 0),
8XY6 SHR Vx (VF = least significant bit of Vx before shift, Vx >>=1),
8XY7 SUBN Vx,Vy (Vx=Vy-Vx, VF = 1 if Vy>=Vx else 0),
8XYE SHL Vx (VF = most significant bit of Vx before shift, Vx <<=1),
9XY0 SNE Vx,Vy, ANNN LD I,addr, BNNN JP V0,addr, CXNN RND Vx,byte (random 0-255 AND byte),
DXYN DRW Vx,Vy,n — draw sprite from memory[I..I+n-1] at (Vx,Vy), XOR onto display with wraparound off (clip at edges or wrap — wrap modulo 64/32 for starting coords, clip the drawing is fine), set VF=1 if any pixel flipped from set to unset (collision), else VF=0; mark display as dirty for redraw,
EX9E SKP Vx (skip next instr if key in Vx is pressed), EXA1 SKNP Vx (skip if NOT pressed),
FX07 LD Vx,DT, FX0A LD Vx,K (blocking wait for a keypress — halt PC advance until a key is pressed, then store it in Vx; implement via an internal 'waiting for key' flag checked in the key handler, do not busy-loop),
FX15 LD DT,Vx, FX18 LD ST,Vx, FX1E ADD I,Vx, FX29 LD F,Vx (I = 0x050 + Vx*5),
FX33 BCD (store BCD of Vx at I, I+1, I+2), FX55 LD [I],Vx (store V0..Vx into memory starting at I, classic behavior: do not modify I), FX65 LD Vx,[I] (load V0..Vx from memory starting at I).
Unknown opcodes should be logged/ignored gracefully without crashing.

DEMO ROM: Embed this exact byte array as the built-in demo program (do not change these bytes — it is a hand-assembled real CHIP-8 program that draws a 5-row sprite at (10,10) and, while key '6' is held, erases and redraws the sprite moving one pixel right per frame using XOR draw, looping via SKNP key test):
const DEMO_ROM = new Uint8Array([
  0x60,0x0A, 0x61,0x0A, 0xA2,0x18, 0xD0,0x15, 0x62,0x06, 0xE2,0xA1, 0x12,0x10, 0x12,0x0A,
  0xD0,0x15, 0x70,0x01, 0xD0,0x15, 0x12,0x0A,
  0x3C,0x42,0xA5,0x81,0x42
]);
Load this ROM by default on page load / on Reset (reset should reload whichever ROM is currently active — demo or last-loaded file).

ROM LOADING FROM FILE: a <input type="file"> control; on file selection, read as ArrayBuffer (FileReader), convert to Uint8Array, store as "current ROM bytes", reset the whole machine state and load it at 0x200, keep running/paused state as it was (start paused after load, require pressing Run).

CONTROLS (all must be real working UI elements, not decorative):
- Run button: starts the execution loop (uses requestAnimationFrame; each frame executes N instructions where N = instructions-per-frame, then renders display if dirty).
- Pause button: stops the run loop (cancel the rAF), keeps state.
- Single Step button: executes exactly one instruction (decode+execute), works whether running or paused (if running, pause it first), updates debugger panel and canvas immediately.
- Reset button: reinitializes memory/registers/stack/timers/display/keys, reloads the font at 0x050 and the current ROM (demo or last loaded file) at 0x200, PC=0x200, pauses.
- Speed control: a number input or range slider for "instructions per frame" (e.g. range 1-500, default ~10), label showing current value, live-updates the loop's per-frame instruction count.
- Run/Pause state should be reflected in the UI (e.g. disable Run while running, disable Pause while paused, or a status label "Running"/"Paused").

DEBUGGER PANEL (updates every frame while running, and on step/reset/pause):
- All 16 registers V0-VF shown in hex, labeled.
- I register in hex.
- PC in hex.
- DT and ST values.
- The call stack contents (addresses) and stack pointer.
- The current/just-decoded instruction: raw opcode hex (4 hex digits) and a short human-readable mnemonic/disassembly string (e.g. "DRW V0, V1, 5").

STYLING: Clean dark-themed UI, monospace font for debugger/hex values, reasonably organized layout (canvas + keypad on one side, controls + debugger on the other, can stack vertically on narrow viewport). No external fonts/icons/images.

Make sure the whole thing is valid, self-contained, working vanilla JS (no frameworks), in one HTML file named exactly as requested. Write the complete file now.
"}
